name: whois
one_line: look up who owns a domain name or IP address
plain: `whois` asks a public registry who registered a domain or owns an IP range: organisation, registrar, creation date, name servers, abuse contact. Modern registrations often hide personal details behind a privacy service, but the dates and name servers are still useful.
It is the first step in passive recon (OSINT): you learn who is behind a target without touching the target.
when: Find who owns a domain and when it was registered.
Find the network range and owner of an IP.
Find name servers and abuse contacts.

examples.title: A domain
examples.explain: Prints registrar, creation and expiry dates, name servers and status. Very new dates on a phishing-looking domain are a red flag.

examples.title: An IP address
examples.explain: Shows the network block, the organisation and the abuse contact for the address.

examples.title: Ask a specific registry
examples.explain: -h chooses the server; useful when the default server sends you to another one.

examples.title: Keep only a few lines
examples.explain: whois output is long; grep keeps the facts you need.

examples.title: Several domains
examples.cmd: for d in a.com b.com; do whois $d | grep -i 'creation date'; done
examples.explain: A small loop to compare registration dates.

mistakes: Treating privacy-protected data as an error: it is normal.
Forgetting that IPs and domains use different registries.
Querying too fast and getting rate-limited.
Using whois data for harassment: use it for research and abuse reports only.
